key_insight: This paper shows how individual words in style instructions shape the sounds produced by a text-to-speech model. By adapting cross-attention attribution to speech, it makes the model’s style-control behavior visible and easier to diagnose.
problem_solved: Style-captioned TTS systems can follow natural-language style prompts, but it is often unclear which words are influencing pitch, rhythm, emotion, or other acoustic traits. This lack of interpretability makes it hard to debug failures and improve controllability.
method: Adapts DAAM-style cross-attention attribution from image generation to speech diffusion models for the first time.
Applies the method to CapSpeech-TTS to produce per-token heatmaps showing how each instruction word affects generated speech.
Aggregates attention across 25 layers to reveal word-level influence patterns and model behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a practical interpretability tool for expressive TTS systems. It can help diagnose when a model ignores, overuses, or misinterprets style instructions, leading to better controllability and more reliable speech generation.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing text style caption -> TTS model -> generated speech with token-level attribution heatmaps.
A heatmap overlay highlighting which words influence different acoustic attributes.
A layer-wise attribution visualization across the 25 diffusion layers.
An icon-based comparison of intended style words versus realized speech properties.
paper_title: How Do Instructions Shape Speech? Cross-Attention Attribution for Style-Captioned Text-to-Speech
paper_authors: Nityanand Mathur, Hamees Sayed, Wasim Madha, Apoorv Singh, Sameer Khurana
